title: Number of Provinces
prompt:
There are `n` cities. Some of them are directly connected, while others are not. A province is a group of directly or indirectly connected cities, with no other cities outside the group.

You are given an `n x n` matrix `isConnected` where `isConnected[i][j] = 1` if the `i`th city and `j`th city are directly connected, and `0` otherwise. Return the total number of provinces.

examples.explanation: Cities 0 and 1 are directly connected, forming one province; city 2 is isolated, forming its own province.
No two cities are connected, so each city is its own province.
A single city (with only the required self-connection) forms exactly one province by itself.

hints: This is exactly counting connected components, just with the graph given as an adjacency matrix instead of an edge list.
Pick an unvisited city, DFS (or BFS) to every city reachable through direct connections, mark them all visited, and count that as one province.
Union-Find also works cleanly: union every pair (i, j) where isConnected[i][j] == 1, then count the number of distinct roots.

solution.approach: Treat isConnected as an adjacency matrix and run DFS from every unvisited city, marking every city reachable via direct connections (rows with a 1) as visited and belonging to the current province. Each time we start a DFS from a fresh unvisited city, that's a new province, since every city already reachable from a previous DFS is already marked visited.
